thread:
Ava: FYI customer CS-2091 reports intermittent connection resets to our Private VPC hostname through their corporate TLS proxy. Started after their TLS profile was tightened.
Jena: Do we have the client-side error? curl/openssl output would help.
Ava: Their app logs show: "error: write EPROTO ...: SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert protocol version" and lots of ECONNRESET on retries.
Sam: Sounds like TLS negotiation failure — protocol_version alert. Ask for openssl s_client dumps for tls1.2 and tls1.3, and a tcpdump if possible.
Ava: Customer attached these. Their default s_client (no -tls flag) gets alert 70. TLS1.2 succeeds, TLS1.3 fails. Snippet:
```
$ openssl s_client -connect private.redwood.internal:443 -servername private.redwood.internal
CONNECTED(00000003)
1407A9...:error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert protocol version:s3_pkt.c:1493:SSL alert number 70
```
Jena: Alert 70 maps to protocol_version. Could be the proxy or our edge refusing a negotiated version/cipher. Do they terminate TLS (re-encrypt) or passthrough?
Mike: They say the proxy is in re-encrypt (MITM) mode and applied a stricter profile last week. They claim upstream profile is still compat, but TLS1.3 attempts still fail.
Sam: Two main hypotheses: 1) Proxy strips TLS1.3 or rewrites ClientHello in a way our edge rejects; 2) Proxy re-encrypts upstream with an RSA-only/RSA-preferred cipher list and our endpoint now prefers ECDSA/TLS1.3-only ciphers after a recent config roll.
Ava: I asked them to run:
- curl -v --resolve private.redwood.internal:443:10.0.0.5 https://private.redwood.internal/health
- openssl s_client -connect private.redwood.internal:443 -tls1_2 -servername private.redwood.internal
- openssl s_client -connect private.redwood.internal:443 -tls1_3 -servername private.redwood.internal
- and to capture proxy->upstream s_client and client->proxy tcpdump

Customer reply: curl forced to --tlsv1.2 works, default fails. Attached s_client outputs show TLS1.2 completes, TLS1.3 triggers protocol_version alert from upstream.

Customer s_client (proxy->upstream) shows proxy attempting TLS1.3 but server replies alert:
```
$ openssl s_client -connect 10.0.0.5:443 -servername private.redwood.internal -tls1_3
CONNECTED(00000003)
write:errno=104
1407B1...:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert protocol version
```
Jena: We recently changed the ingress to prefer TLS1.3 and ECDSA curves for perf. If their proxy is MITM and presenting a different cert/cipher set, that could explain the mismatch.
Sam: Short-term workarounds:
- Customer can force TLS1.2 on their outbound calls (e.g., --tlsv1.2). Immediate but not ideal.
- They can change proxy to passthrough our traffic (often blocked by enterprise policy).

Longer-term options we can offer:
1) Provision a compatibility listener for Private endpoints that accepts TLS1.2 and a wider RSA cipher suite for specific customers (temporary).
2) Issue an alternate hostname/IP that presents an RSA-signed cert and TLS1.2-friendly ciphers (needs infra + cert work).
3) Roll back the global TLS preference (undesirable blanket change).

Mike: Customer asked if this was a change on our side. We confirmed the ingress preference update was rolled last week. They want a targeted compatibility fix.

Sam: I'll draft an RFC for a per-customer compatibility listener (include ACLs, logging, short TTL, rate limits). Need eng-infra & security signoff.
Jena: Also request ALPN debug from customer (s_client -alpn "h2,http/1.1") to check if ALPN/h2 is being stripped — can cause other fallbacks.
Ava: Added ALPN ask and requested pcap + both s_client outputs. Updated ticket and escalated.

ticket-bot: Ticket CS-2091 updated: assigned to eng-infra/sam. Priority: High. Workarounds provided.
infra-bot: Ingress logs during window show entries: "tls_alert: protocol_version (70)" and several peer_reset records for the client subnet.

Ava: Customer accepted temporary client-side TLS1.2 workaround while we scope infra change. Marked ETA for RFC within 3 business days.
Sam: Pinged infra leads to review feasibility of presenting RSA chain per-host and adding a compatibility listener behind ACL.
Jena: Note: include explicit test plan in RFC (s_client tls1.2 and tls1.3, ALPN, cert chain checks) and rollback criteria.
Ava: Thanks all. Will keep ticket updated. :white_check_mark:
